outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Large Language Model (LLM) Finetuning
outline.description: This chapter provides context on the current state of LLMs, the necessity of finetuning for specialized tasks, and the primary hardware bottlenecks that hinder the training of massive models.
subtopics: The role of finetuning in LLM behavior modification
Memory constraints: Comparing 16-bit finetuning requirements to available hardware
The limitations of standard quantization in training contexts
Overview of the QLoRA objective: High-fidelity 4-bit finetuning

outline.description: A deep dive into the mathematical and architectural foundations upon which QLoRA is built, specifically block-wise quantization and Low-Rank Adapters.
subtopics: Block-wise k-bit Quantization: Scaling, rounding, and the outlier problem
Dequantization processes and the role of quantization constants
Low-Rank Adapters (LoRA): The factorized projection approach
Memory analysis: Comparing adapter weights vs. activation gradients
Gradient checkpointing and its impact on memory management

outline.description: This chapter explains the three core technical contributions of the QLoRA paper designed to save memory without sacrificing model performance.
subtopics: 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4): Information-theoretically optimal data types for normal distributions
Quantile Quantization and the derivation of the NF4 data type
Double Quantization: Reducing the memory footprint of quantization constants
Paged Optimizers: Leveraging NVIDIA unified memory to manage memory spikes
The QLoRA Forward and Backward Pass: Integrating NF4, Double Quantization, and LoRA

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Analysis: QLoRA vs. Standard Finetuning
outline.description: An analysis of experimental results comparing QLoRA to full 16-bit finetuning and standard LoRA, establishing the validity of the proposed method.
subtopics: Comparative benchmarks across different architectures (Encoder, Decoder, Encoder-Decoder)
The importance of LoRA adapter placement (all linear layers vs. Query/Value only)
Hyperparameter sensitivity: Learning rates, batch sizes, and projection dimensions
Evaluating NF4 precision: Comparing NF4 against FP4 and Int4
Performance recovery: Demonstrating that 4-bit QLoRA matches 16-bit performance

outline.chapter_title: Instruction Tuning and the Guanaco Model Family
outline.description: A study of instruction finetuning at scale, detailing the creation of the Guanaco models and the analysis of dataset quality.
subtopics: Instruction tuning datasets: OASST1, Alpaca, FLAN v2, and others
The Guanaco Model Family: Achieving ChatGPT-level performance on a single GPU
Data Quality vs. Dataset Size: Why smaller, high-quality datasets can outperform larger ones
Orthogonality of benchmarks: Why MMLU performance does not guarantee chatbot success
Training Guanaco on 33B and 65B parameter models

outline.chapter_title: Advanced Evaluation Methodologies and Qualitative Analysis
outline.description: This chapter explores how to measure the success of chatbots using both automated and human metrics, and provides a qualitative look at model behaviors.
subtopics: GPT-4 as an automated evaluator: Reliability and order effects
Human evaluation protocols and Elo rating systems for chatbot tournaments
Qualitative analysis: Factual recall, suggestibility, and refusal behaviors
Model limitations: Mathematical reasoning and Theory of Mind
The problem of benchmark validity and 'shortcuts'

outline.description: Concluding the textbook by discussing the societal impacts of QLoRA, including democratization of AI and potential mobile applications.
subtopics: Democratizing LLM research: Closing the resource gap between corporations and small teams
On-device finetuning: The possibility of training models on mobile phones
Dual-use concerns: The risks of widespread, accessible finetuning
Future research: 3-bit precision, different adapter types, and responsibility in AI
